questions.stem: Which term correctly defines a word root in medical terminology?

options.text: An element added to the end of a word to change its meaning
A letter inserted between word parts to make pronunciation easier
The foundational element that carries the core meaning of a medical word
An element added to the front of a word to modify its meaning

Identifying the root first is the standard strategy for decoding unfamiliar terms.

questions.stem: Which statement accurately describes the position and function of a prefix?

options.text: It follows the root to name a condition, procedure, or descriptive state
It precedes the root to modify meaning such as number, location, or time
It links two separate word roots together to smooth out pronunciation

questions.stem: Why is a combining vowel (usually 'o') inserted between two word parts?

options.text: To change the meaning of the root from a singular form to a plural form
To signal that the element which follows is a prefix rather than a suffix
To ease pronunciation when linking a root to another root or a consonant suffix
To indicate that the overall term is describing an abnormal body condition

rationales.whyCorrect: The combining vowel, most often 'o,' is used to make a term easier to pronounce when a root is joined to a suffix that begins with a consonant or to another root (as in gastr-o-enterology).
